title: Astra - "Critical" for cyber, called the start of the "AGI era" - stumbles on release - TCR 09/04/26
description:
OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra, its first model rated Critical for cyber capability, alongside a $1 billion Daybreak defender fund, ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini suffered near-simultaneous outages across a single Thursday morning, and a gene-edited pig kidney kept a man off dialysis for a record 271 days before a clean handoff to a human transplant.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-4-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:45 GPT-6 Astra ships with a defender fund
5:19 Four frontier models go dark at once
7:44 Flock's AI watchlist and the pushback
10:49 A pig kidney bridges to a human transplant
13:39 An AI builds materials atom by atom
16:03 Close

This episode covers OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra launch and its AGI-era claim, the four-provider AI outage and the shared substrate beneath it, WIRED's reconstruction of Flock's AI watchlist as Texas and Florida pull the cameras, eGenesis's pig kidney bridge to human transplant, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's 25-hour unsupervised atom-by-atom fabrication, IFM's fully reproducible K2 Horizon models, and China's Q2 oil-driven emissions decline.

OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra to paid and enterprise customers on Thursday, its first model rated Critical for cyber capability, and cofounder Greg Brockman declared the AGI era open as the company races toward a public offering. Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki offered the more candid note, conceding that monitoring what these systems do internally is getting harder and may constrain further scaling. Hours later, ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini faltered inside a single morning; providers marketed as rivals can depend on overlapping infrastructure. WIRED rebuilt Flock's newest AI watchlist from the code it ships to police browsers, a webinar showed officers aiming it at a No Kings protest, and Texas and Florida moved to pull the cameras. eGenesis reported a gene-edited pig kidney that kept Tim Andrews off dialysis for a record 271 days before a handoff to a human transplant, with the published case showing no new antibodies against human tissue. And an AI at Oak Ridge National Laboratory fabricated custom materials atom by atom for more than 25 hours unsupervised, locking 37 molecules into working artificial graphene, while IFM published K2 Horizon's full training lifecycle for anyone to reproduce.
